verdict.rationale: A robots.txt is a fair question for any public web service, so the axis applies. The only relevant evidence is the probe, and it does not show a real robots.txt on the e-filing host: it records HTTP 200 but describes the response as a server error, and an earlier observation saw a page with no robots directives. Nothing in the docs mentions a robots.txt or crawler policy for dos.fl.gov either, so an agent cannot learn what it may read before fetching.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service publishes a real robots.txt, so an agent can know what it may read before fetching anything
